titleDv: ޤާނޫނު ނަންބަރު 2/2008 (ވަޒީފާއާބެހޭ ޤާނޫނު) އަށް 9 ވަނަ އިޞްލާޙު ގެނައުމުގެ ބިލު
summary: This is the 9th amendment to the Employment Act, as passed by Parliament. It changes notice rules for ending a job, with 2 weeks' notice for staff employed up to a year and pay allowed instead of notice. Overtime now needs the worker's agreement. Parents get two paid 30-minute breaks a day to go to their child until age two. Cabinet can excuse some small businesses from foreign-worker quota fees. It adds fines for leaking information, impersonating labour officers and false statements.
whyItMatters: Workers get clearer notice and overtime rights, and new parents get paid childcare breaks. Some small businesses may pay less in foreign-worker quota fees, and labour officers must keep information confidential.
keyProvisions: Article 22: an open-ended job contract can only be ended after notice; staff employed for up to one year get 2 weeks' notice, and both sides can agree on a longer or shorter notice period
Article 25: notice can be replaced by paying the salary and benefits for the whole notice period
Article 37: overtime only under an agreement between employer and employee
Article 45: from returning after maternity leave until the child turns 2, two 30-minute breaks a day to go to the child, with no pay cut
Article 65-4: the Cabinet may exempt certain small and medium businesses from foreign-worker quota fees, to support SMEs, long-term jobs and innovation

Articles 84-86-3: labour officers must keep information confidential (fine MVR 5,000-25,000); impersonating an officer fined MVR 25,000-100,000; giving the Authority false information fined MVR 15,000-100,000; fines paid to MIRA. Article 97 updates the public holiday list to include International Workers' Day
whoIsAffected: All employees and employers covered by the Employment Act, new parents, small and medium businesses, and the Labour Relations Authority.
